transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

I guess… I came in because I keep feeling like I’ve ruined things for everybody. Like at my apprenticeship, I feel like I’m fake, like I shouldn’t be there, even though other people probably mess stuff up and just fix it and move on.

And then I start thinking I let my family down too, and even the younger apprentices, which sounds kind of dramatic when I say it out loud. I don’t know. It just keeps sitting on me.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once liked?

Yeah… I think so. Like, I used to sketch a lot, and I’ll literally walk past my sketchbook now and just not pick it up. Same with volleyball—I’ve been skipping it, and the volunteer group chat keeps buzzing and I just ignore it.

It’s weird because those were kind of my things, like the stuff that made me feel normal or like myself, you know? Now it’s just… I don’t feel much about them.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it “most of the day, nearly every day.” I mean, I have these stretches where I feel really low, especially when I’m just sitting there and thinking too much, but then sometimes I’m just distracted at work or someone says something dumb and I laugh for a second.

It’s hard to measure, I guess. Like, what counts as depressed versus just tired or stressed? Sorry, I’m kind of circling it. I’ve noticed feeling down, yeah, but I’m not totally sure how often.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or that you’ve let others down more than you actually have?

Yeah… that’s probably the biggest thing, honestly. I keep feeling like I’ve messed everything up for everyone, even when it’s something small. Like at the apprenticeship, I’ll make a mistake and it turns into this whole thing in my head where I’m like, “I’m a fake, I shouldn’t be here.”

And then somehow it spreads, like I start thinking I’ve let my family down, and even the younger apprentices, which is weird because they’re not even asking that of me. I know other people would probably just fix the issue and move on, but I get stuck on it like it means something about me.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or that you’ve let others down more than you actually have, on most days lately?

Yeah… most days lately, I think. That’s kind of what made me come in, honestly. I keep getting stuck in this thing where I feel like I ruined stuff for everybody, even when it’s not that big.

Like at the apprenticeship, if I mess something up, I start feeling like I’m a fake and I shouldn’t even be there. And then my brain goes off into, like, “you let your family down,” or even the younger apprentices, which doesn’t totally make sense because they’re not sitting there saying that to me. I know someone else would probably just fix it and move on, but I don’t. I just carry it around.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the time, nearly every day, for as long as you can remember—like, has this been going on for two years or more?

No, not two years or anything like that. It’s more like… maybe nine months? Around there. It kind of crept in, so it’s hard to pin down exactly.

I guess it got more obvious when school and work started slipping, because before that I could sort of cover it up or just tell myself I was tired. I mean, everyone’s tired in this trade, right? But yeah, not as long as I can remember. More like this past year, but not the whole year.
Have you had days where you feel down or low most of the time, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… definitely more than two weeks. It’s been kind of this long stretch, like around nine months, where I’ve felt low a lot of the time.

It’s weird because at first I could sort of hide it, or I’d blame it on being busy or tired. In the trades everyone’s always saying they’re tired, and school stuff piles up, and then you’ve got work and people expecting you to just keep moving. But once school and work started slipping, it got harder to pretend it was just normal stress.
Have you had a depressed mood most of the time, nearly every day, for at least two years at a time?

No, not two years. I know it probably feels like I keep circling around that, sorry. It’s been more like about nine months where the low mood has been there a lot, most days.

It got harder to kind of pass off once school and work started slipping. Before that I’d just be like, “Oh, I’m tired,” or blame the schedule, because everybody does that. But… yeah, not two years. More like this stretch since sometime this past year.
Have you had days where you feel down or low most of the time, nearly every day, for at least two years at a time?

No, not two years. I know I’ve kind of said that already, but it’s more like… around nine months.

It kind of sat there in the background for a while, and I could blame it on being busy or tired or whatever. Then once school and work started slipping, it was harder to act like nothing was going on. But no, not two years at a time.
Have you felt like you’ve had no energy or that you’ve been really tired most of the time during these low mood periods?

I don’t know if I’d say “no energy” exactly. Like, I get tired, but I also work with my hands and I’m on my feet a lot, so it’s hard to tell what’s normal tired and what’s… I don’t know, something else.

Some days I’ll come home and just kind of sit there longer than I meant to, but then I think, well, anyone would be wiped after crawling around under sinks or hauling stuff. And then school stuff is its own kind of exhausting too. So… I’ve noticed being tired, yeah, but I’m not sure if it’s most of the time or if I’m just blaming everything on the schedule.
Have you felt like you're not good enough, or that you're a failure, even when others don't see you that way?

Yeah… I do. That’s kind of one of the bigger reasons I came in, actually.

I keep getting stuck on this feeling like I’ve ruined things for everybody, even when, if someone else did the same thing, I’d probably tell them, “Just fix it and move on.” But when it’s me, it feels like proof I shouldn’t be there. Like I’m fake in the apprenticeship, like everyone else belongs and I’m just waiting for them to notice I don’t.

And then I think about my family, or even the younger apprentices watching what I do, and I feel like I’m letting them down. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, because it’s not like one mistake ends the world. But it feels that way in my head sometimes.
Have you felt a loss of pleasure in most or all activities that you used to enjoy, most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. It’s weird because I still know I used to like those things, but lately I’ll walk right past my sketchbook and just not pick it up. And volleyball too — I’ll tell myself I should go, because once I’m there it’s usually good, or it used to be, anyway, but then I just… don’t.

Same with the volunteer group texts. They’ll pop up, and I used to be the person who answered right away, helped organize stuff, all that. Now I see them and just kind of let them sit there. It’s not even always that I feel upset about it, it’s more like I don’t feel much of anything, which almost bothers me more.

Sorry, I know that’s a little off track. But yeah, the stuff that made me feel like me doesn’t really seem to do much lately.
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been moving really slowly, or that even simple tasks feel like they take forever to get through?

Yeah, a little. Mostly at work I notice it. Like I’ll be on a job and something simple—climbing down to grab a fitting or answering the foreman when he asks me something—feels like it takes way more effort than it should.

And it’s embarrassing because plumbing stuff already has this rhythm to it, you know, like everyone’s moving around and you don’t want to be the one slowing it down. I’ll catch myself just… moving slow. Not on purpose. And a couple people have asked if I’m sick or hungover, which I hated, because I’m like, no, I’m just trying to get through the morning.

So yeah, not every second, but enough that other people have noticed.
Have you noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than usual, to the point where others might notice it?

Yeah, I think so. Mostly at work, honestly. I’ll catch myself moving slower than I mean to, like climbing down just to grab a fitting feels like this whole extra effort thing, which is ridiculous because I do that all the time.

And sometimes the foreman asks me something simple and I take a beat too long to answer, like my mouth is catching up or something. It’s embarrassing because on a job site everyone notices when you’re off your pace. A couple people have asked if I’m sick or hungover, which… I wasn’t. So yeah, I guess it’s noticeable.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite or weight during these low mood periods?

Um… I don’t think I’ve noticed anything major there. My appetite’s maybe kind of all over the place, but I haven’t really been tracking it.

Like some days I’ll forget to eat until I’m already at work and then just grab something stupid from a gas station, but I kind of do that anyway depending on the job site. There’s this one place near a site we were on that had these breakfast burritos that were actually really good, and I kept meaning to ask what sauce they used—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

Weight-wise, I don’t think there’s been some big change. My jeans fit about the same, I guess. So… not really, or at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you felt like you’re worthless or that you’ve been blaming yourself for things that weren’t entirely your fault?

Yeah… that’s actually kind of the main thing that made me come in, I think. I keep getting this feeling like I’ve ruined things for everybody, even when, if I say it out loud, it probably sounds dramatic.

Like with the apprenticeship, I start thinking I’m a fake, like somebody’s going to realize I shouldn’t be there. And if I mess something up—something another person would probably just fix and move on from—I’ll carry it around like I let everyone down. My family, the younger apprentices, people who are counting on me to not be useless.

And I know plumbing jobs always have stuff that goes wrong. Like, that’s literally part of it, you adjust and fix it. My journeyman says that all the time, “just solve the next problem,” and he has this whole thing about not standing around staring at copper like it insulted your mother—sorry, that’s not really the point.

But yeah. I blame myself way more than makes sense. It feels like I’m disappointing everyone.
Have you ever felt that your mood is worse in the morning, or that you feel particularly slowed down or physically heavy early in the day?

Yeah, I mean… I notice it more early in the day when I’m getting going, especially once I’m at work. It’s like my body’s got a delay on it.

I’ll be doing something normal, like climbing down to grab a fitting, and it feels like way more effort than it should. Or the foreman asks me something and I know the answer, but I answer a second too slow, like I’m loading or something. Which is not great on a job site, because everyone’s watching everyone’s pace.

A couple guys have even asked if I was sick or hungover, and I wasn’t. I hate that, because then I start trying to act normal, which somehow makes me feel weirder. So… yeah, I guess physically slowed down, especially getting started.
Have you ever noticed that your mood improves a little when something good happens, even if you're feeling down most of the time?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to it in that exact way.

Like, if something good happens, I might feel okay for a minute—like if someone at work says I did a clean job on something, or if I get coffee and it’s actually made right, which sounds stupid but some places really mess it up. There was this one gas station that had the worst coffee machine, like it tasted burned no matter what button you pressed—

Sorry. I don’t know if my mood “improves” exactly, or if I’m just distracted for a little bit. I guess I haven’t noticed a clear pattern.
